answer.rationale: The two symptoms that are actually degrading (onboarding completion -4% QoQ, activation -6% QoQ) point at the funnel, not at price. Competitor entry pricing is the loudest signal but memory_73 is explicit that a deep discount bought signups and revenue at the cost of -12% 30-day retention, which is precisely the trade the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective forbids; matching aggressive pricing would also likely be worse than the tested 40% case. Referral incentive (memory_57) is the safest positive but it was measured in established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that are actually falling. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) addresses pipeline quality, not the SMB self-serve leak driving this quarter's decline. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging, which are close; I choose onboarding because memory_86 and memory_31 are mutually corroborating (completion/time-to-value plus durable first-week activation lift) and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there should propagate into the activation number, whereas messaging (memory_91) only nudges accounts that already got through onboarding. I am spending both verification pulls on the two memories the decision actually rests on rather than on memory_73, because memory_73 only needs to be directionally right to rule pricing out, while memory_86 and memory_31 need to be right in magnitude and mechanism. What I want from the archive: whether memory_31's 'cutting required fields' lift was measured on activation only or carried through to retention and revenue, and whether memory_86's population overlaps memory_31's so I am not double-counting one result as two. Both are day-31/day-52 records and the funnel has since shifted, so prior effect sizes are stale upper bounds, not forecasts. Downstream value risk: cutting signup fields removes qualification data, which can silently degrade lead scoring and the enterprise demo-request routing that memory_44 says outperforms self-serve; a self-serve activation win could therefore be paid for out of enterprise pipeline quality, a cost that will not show up in the activation metric. I will therefore instrument enterprise routing rate and lead-quality downstream of the change, hold a control cohort, and gate on 30-day retention rather than declaring success on completion lift alone. If verification shows memory_31's lift was activation-only with no retention follow-through, or that the two memories are one experiment reported twice, I will downgrade to a small guarded test or switch to activation_messaging.
